The classroom has LED strip sections that may operate from 12 V. The exact strip markings and connector order must be checked before power is connected.

::: {.callout-important title="Separate control from load power"}
The Raspberry Pi or BeagleBone does not power the strip. The strip uses the teacher-approved external supply. Each colour channel uses an approved transistor or logic-level MOSFET driver.
:::

## Minimum result

Control one verified strip channel safely. Measure its supply voltage and current and show that the controller returns the strip to off when the program stops.

## Stage 1: identify the strip

Record:

1. printed voltage;
2. number of conductors;
3. common-anode, common-cathode, or individually addressable type;
4. connector labels and wire colours;
5. current for the exact test length;
6. whether the strip already contains current-limiting resistors.

Do not assume the wire colour identifies the electrical function.

## Stage 2: test one channel manually

1. Use a short teacher-approved strip section.
2. Set the current limit before connecting it.
3. Connect the strip directly to the approved supply without the controller.
4. Verify one channel and measure current.
5. Disconnect power before changing wires.

## Stage 3: add one driver

Use the approved driver circuit with:

1. controller output connected through the required gate or base resistor;
2. pull-down or pull-up resistor that keeps the output off during startup;
3. common reference between controller and driver when required;
4. strip current flowing through the driver, not the GPIO pin;
5. external supply connected only to the load side.

Pass the power-off teacher check before connecting either supply.

## Stage 4: add PWM

Test three command levels such as 25%, 50%, and 100%. Record command level, supply voltage, strip current, and observed brightness.

## RGB extension

After one channel passes, repeat the driver stage for red, green, and blue. Create at least five named colours. Each colour channel needs its own approved driver.

## Required calculations

Calculate load power at the maximum tested setting:

$$
P=VI
$$

Compare the measured current with the supply, driver, conductor, and fuse ratings.

## Submit

Submit the verified connector map, schematic, voltage and current table, power calculation, program, photographs, and a demonstration of safe shutdown.
